name: Shibuya
description: Sangenjaya to Shibuya, Harajuku and Yoyogi Park from open data, lit by the real sun: Project PLATEAU's surveyed heights, the scramble and Hachiko, SHIBUYA SKY 229 m up, Center Gai, Shibuya Stream and the streets Persona 5 drew.

terrain_check.name: GSI elevation API (1 m laser DEM where flown, otherwise DEM5)

plateau.attribution: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)

water.note: No sea and no open river: the Shibuya River runs in a culvert under the station, and the ponds of Shinjuku Gyoen and Meiji Jingu are left to the aerial photo, since the viewer's water plane sits at sea level and the ground here is 20-45 m above it.

trees.note: Species are not mapped. Elms stand for the zelkovas (keyaki) of Omotesando and the shrine groves, plane trees for the street planes and ginkgos of Aoyama and Meiji Jingu Gaien. A guess, not a survey.

tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height that Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's laser-scanned bare earth under GSI aerial photographs.

tour.title: The scramble
tour.text: Four streets meet at Shibuya's scramble, and when the lights change every crossing goes green at once, the diagonal too. The white bars are drawn from OpenStreetMap's crosswalks. Hachiko sits on his granite to the south.

tour.title: SHIBUYA SKY, 229 m
tour.text: On Scramble Square's roof (2019): about 2,500 m² of open deck at {landmark:shibuya_sky.deck_m} m, glass at the edge, GEO COMPASS in the middle and the escalator coming up out of the 46th floor.

tour.title: Sangenjaya's triangle
tour.text: Between Setagaya-dori and Route 246, the backstreets of Sangenjaya: a bathhouse, a snack bar, a meat shop open all night. A game drew its home town here and called it Yongen-Jaya.

protection.title: No sun-access rule for public places
protection.summary: Tokyo protects no park's sunlight. The windows are a lunch-hour thought experiment for this project, as in the Marunouchi model.
protection.source_note: Windows are our own choice (noon to 13:00, all year), not law. The Building Standards Act's shadow rule (日影規制, art. 56-2) limits hours of shadow on neighbouring land in residential-type zones; it does not cover public places and does not apply in commercial districts such as Shibuya.
protection.reading_note: Tokyo keeps standard time all year. Miyashita Park is a roof garden on a mall (2020): its sun here is read at the ground, so treat it with care.
protection.tip: Tip: try a tower on the block south of Yoyogi Park, west of Harajuku Station.

game.title: Tokyo Pilgrimage: Shibuya 東京巡礼・渋谷
game.blurb: Walk Shibuya under the real sun: the scramble and Hachiko, SHIBUYA SKY 229 m up, Center Gai and Sangenjaya's backstreets, ten years after a game made them famous.

crowd.note: hours: the share of the peak crowd out, by the hour: the morning commute, lunch, and the evening, busiest from 18:00 to 21:00 and busier still on Friday and Saturday nights and at the weekend (Shibuya Redevelopment Association, 2014: 260,000 people a day on weekdays, 390,000 on holidays); few after the last trains (about 00:30)

look.note: neon: the screens' light on the street (web/neon.js); fill: after dark, the light the crossing's shopfronts, floodlights and signs put on the middle of the scramble, where no street lamp stands (a light card over it, medium and high tiers); sound: the crossing's murmur, its screens' music, the walk signal's bird calls and the station's announcements (web/game/audio.js)

idle: Ten years since a film and a game drew these streets. This October the pilgrims are everywhere.

npcs.name: Shun 駿
idle: Center Gai never sleeps. It does get quieter around five in the morning.
The arch is real, the burger bar isn't. People still ask.

npcs.name: Yuna 優奈
idle: Lifts from 14F to 45F at 360 metres a minute. Your ears may pop.
The roof closes in strong wind or lightning. Today: {sun_line}

npcs.name: Taro 太郎
idle: Golden hour at SKY EDGE: the towers go copper, then the scramble lights up.

npcs.name: Haru 晴
idle: Sancha, everybody calls it. Three tea houses on the Oyama road, once.
The Setagaya Line's little trams start from the Carrot Tower.

npcs.name: Mr Tanaka 田中さん
npcs.role: A regular at the sentō 常連
idle: Forty years a regular. The water's hotter on the men's side, they say on the women's side.
A bath, then a cold milk from the machine. That's the rule.

lines.title: Report back
lines.on_open: Every walk done. Report back to Aoi at Hachiko.

quests.title: Hachiko
talk: ようこそ渋谷へ! I'm Aoi. I guide pilgrims: people who come to stand where a story stood. This month it's ten years since a film and a game put these streets on the map.
Hachiko has sat here since 1948. A game called this square Station Square. Walk out onto the scramble when the lights change.
Want to see it from above? The lift at SKY GATE in Scramble Square, just across the road, goes up to SHIBUYA SKY, and a helicopter waits on the roof. A hand up at the kerb (Y) stops a taxi.

steps.text: Meet Shun at the mouth of Center Gai

quests.title: Center Gai
talk: Center Gai. A game called it Central Street and gave it a burger bar that doesn't exist. The arch is real: go and read it.
See the glass passage over the crossing, on the station side? Okamoto Taro's thirty-metre mural, Myth of Tomorrow, hangs inside. A game made that passage a hideout.
For the view everyone came for, go up SHIBUYA SKY on top of Scramble Square. Yuna works the door.

steps.text: Read the arch over Center Gai
Find Yuna at SHIBUYA SKY's street door

quests.title: SHIBUYA SKY
talk: SKY GATE: the lifts run from 14F to 45F at 360 metres a minute. From the 46th floor an escalator takes you out into the open air.
The roof is about 2,500 square metres. The glass is lowest at SKY EDGE, over the scramble. No bags past 46F: the wind takes them.
Press E by the lift door. Or open the map: the roof is on your list of places to go.

steps.text: Ride the escalator out onto the roof
Stand at SKY EDGE, over the scramble

quests.title: SKY EDGE
talk: From up here the scramble is a clock face: everyone waits, then everyone goes.
GEO COMPASS, the raised deck in the middle, points at places you can't see: Mt Fuji, Skytree, Suga Shrine, even Paris and Sydney.
After dark, CROSSING LIGHT: eighteen searchlights. {sun_line}

quests.title: Sangenjaya
talk: Sangenjaya, three tea houses. In a game it's Yongen-Jaya, four: the same backstreets with one more tea house.
The game's café has the front of a snack bar here, New Marina. The bathhouse is Chiyo-no-yu, across the lane.
Take it slow. These are people's homes and small shops.

quests.title: Chiyo-no-yu
talk: Forty years a regular. The curtain says ゆ: hot water. Men on one side, women on the other.
Coin laundry beside it, vending machines out front. Everything a backstreet needs.
Come back after dark. The signs light up the triangle between Setagaya-dori and Route 246.

quests.title: Pilgrim
talk: お帰り! A crossing, a bathhouse, a roof 229 metres up. All of it real, and now you've stood in all of it.

Ten years ago a game drew these streets. Now you've walked them. The stairs of Your Name are in Shinjuku: two stops north on the Yamanote Line, and my friend Nao guides there. Or change the time, go up SHIBUYA SKY at night, or just wander.
